title: Adaptive prefetch lease model and cancellation orchestration for Go SDK streaming
creator: Avery Kim
description: Introduce an adaptive prefetch "lease" model in the Go SDK streaming client to improve tail latency and reduce wasted tokens while making cancellation semantics explicit and deterministic. Current problems: (1) fixed prefetch windows either underfill (hurting latency) or overfetch (wasting tokens/cost), (2) cancellation races between client shutdown and server-side in-flight token emission cause unclear resource accounting and occasionally duplicate work, (3) multiplexed connections with multiple logical streams have brittle cancellation coordination. This ticket proposes: a token-lease abstraction, dynamic window sizing based on observed token emission rate and latency, a lease revocation handshake with the server for graceful drain, and SDK ergonomics that make it easy for callers to request immediate cancellation vs. graceful drain-of-prefetch. The goal is low-latency streaming for interactive apps and predictable accounting for billed tokens in cancelled flows.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a 'Lease' object in Go SDK that grants N prefetch tokens to a stream and can be revoked by client or server with an observable 'Drain' phase
Adaptive window algorithm adjusts prefetch size within +/−30% of median observed emission rate and reduces size by at least 2x within 200ms of sustained slowdowns
Cancellation API with two modes: ImmediateCancel() and DrainThenClose(ctx, timeout) exposed in Go SDK examples
Add unit and integration tests that simulate slow emitter, fast emitter, mid-stream cancellation, and multiplexed streams under contention

Update docs and add example code in repository's examples/ directory demonstrating graceful shutdown in a typical HTTP handler: 1) request cancellation on client disconnect 2) request DrainThenClose with 500ms timeout
Benchmark shows <=10% regression in steady-state throughput and >=20% reduction in wasted tokens for bursty workloads compared to fixed-window baseline
technical_notes: Design: introduce client.Lease struct { Tokens int; ID string; ExpiresAt time.Time } and client.StreamLeaseManager responsible for allotting leases per-connection.

Lease semantics: lease.Tokens is a soft prefetch credit. When revoked, stream enters Drain state: server continues to emit up to remaining tokens but will not start new speculative generations. Client can call DrainThenClose(ctx, timeout) to wait until tokens are consumed or timeout elapses.

Adaptive algorithm: maintain EWMA of emission rate (tokens/ms) and a short-term variance window. Target prefetch = clamp(ceil(EWMA * target_latency_ms), min=1, max=64). target_latency_ms default = 25ms; tunable via WithPrefetchConfig() option.

Cancellation: ImmediateCancel() sends a RevocationRequest over the control channel and transitions local stream to Closed; it also records revocation in telemetry with fields {reason, tokens_revoked, time_to_ack}. DrainThenClose negotiates and waits for DrainComplete or timeout before closing; returns a structured error ErrDrainTimedOut if timed out.

Multiplexing: when multiple logical streams share a TCP/HTTP/QUIC connection, StreamLeaseManager tracks per-stream credits and a shared connection budget. On heavy contention prefer short leases and fair round-robin refill. Implement backpressure: if connection budget exhausted, stall new prefetch until drain frees credits.

Server changes: control-plane support required: Accept RevocationRequest and respond with DrainAck; optional DrainComplete once remaining tokens emitted. We will provide a compatibility shim: if server lacks DrainAck, client falls back to immediate close after best-effort cancellation and emits a compatibility telemetry tag.
Telemetry: record fields tokens_requested, tokens_granted, tokens_consumed, cancel_mode, drain_duration_ms, ack_latency_ms. Use these for automatic config tuning in future Optimize features.

Testing: fuzzed network tests to force out-of-order acks, delayed DrainComplete, and partial emission. Integration test harness uses local test server with controllable emission pace (fast/slow/pulse).

API ergonomics: add examples in godoc and README showing idiomatic patterns: defer cancel on context timeout, prefer DrainThenClose for user-initiated disconnects, ImmediateCancel for critical process shutdowns.
